title: One payment. Three emails.
label: MAYA'S CHECKOUT
voice: Maya pays one hundred and twenty dollars once. Her bank confirms one transaction. Then three order confirmation emails arrive, and the warehouse receives repeated shipping requests.
note: Repeated notifications do not prove repeated charges.

title: The acknowledgement was lost
label: WHAT WENT WRONG?
voice: The payment provider sends a signed success webhook. Our server processes it, but its acknowledgement is lost. The provider cannot tell whether processing finished.
note: A lost reply does not undo the database commit.

title: Retry repeats the unsafe work
label: SAME EVENT, AGAIN
voice: The provider retries the same event. An unsafe handler sends another email and shipment request. The webhook reports an existing payment. It does not charge the customer again.
note: One charge · three deliveries · repeated fulfillment intents

title: First protection: durable inbox
label: VERIFY, THEN ACCEPT
voice: First, verify the original request bytes, timestamp and merchant. Save the event identity in a durable PostgreSQL inbox. A repeated delivery is safely acknowledged without creating new work.
note: Inbox = durable delivery deduplication across restarts and replicas.

title: Second: guard the payment state
label: NEW ID, SAME PAYMENT
voice: A different event identifier can still describe the same payment. Transition pending to succeeded only once. A late success notification must never move a refunded payment back to succeeded.
note: Delivery identity and business identity are different protections.

title: Third: commit a reliable intent
label: OUTBOX + DESTINATION KEYS
voice: Commit the inbox, payment update and outbox intent in one database transaction, then acknowledge. A separate worker retries with stable email and fulfillment keys. Downstream systems must deduplicate too.
note: No external network calls inside the acceptance transaction.

title: One payment. One logical outcome.
label: CUSTOMER PROTECTED
voice: Now repeated webhooks receive a safe acknowledgement without repeating the business action. One payment, one logical confirmation, one fulfillment intent. Monitor failures and reconcile ambiguous outcomes. These are illustrative counts, not production measurements.
note: Outbox intent alone is not exactly-once physical delivery.
